content: Teucrium is a genus of perennial plants that belong to the family Lamiaceae. The name Teucrium is thought to be derived from King Teucer of Troy. Plants within this genus are commonly referred to as germanders. These species can take the form of herbs, shrubs, or subshrubs and are most frequently found in regions with Mediterranean climates. A distinctive characteristic of Teucrium species, compared to other members of the Lamiaceae family, is the complete absence of the upper lip of the corolla in their flowers. While the upper lip is somewhat reduced in other genera within the family, such as Ajuga, it is entirely absent in Teucrium. Several species of Teucrium serve as food sources for the larvae of certain Lepidoptera species, including the Coleophora case-bearers Coleophora auricella and Coleophora chamaedriella. Notably, Coleophora chamaedriella is exclusively associated with Wall Germander (Teucrium chamaedrys). Teucrium species are known to be rich in essential oils. They are appreciated for their ornamental value, their role as a source of pollen, and, in some cases, their culinary and medicinal applications.
